title: Nine Tales by Beatrix Potter
author: Beatrix Potter
blurb: Nine little animal tales: Peter Rabbit in Mr. McGregor’s garden, a cheeky squirrel, two mice in a doll’s house and more. Short sentences and everyday words.
note: The tales came out between 1902 and 1909 and the author died in 1943, so they are in the public domain worldwide. Each tale is its own Project Gutenberg ebook (14838, 14872, 14407, 45264, 14814, 14837, 15077, 15137, 14220). Straight single quotation marks are changed to curly double ones.
coverCredit: Beatrix Potter, Mrs. Rabbit and her children, from The Tale of Peter Rabbit, 1902. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Aesop’s Fables for Children (selection)
author: Aesop
blurb: Fifty fables in simple English, among them the fox and the grapes, the lion and the mouse and the shepherd boy who cried wolf. Each is a page or less and ends with a one-line lesson.
note: This retelling for children was published in 1919, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). It is the first fifty fables of the book; the pictures are left out.
coverCredit: Milo Winter, The Fox and the Grapes, from The Aesop for Children, 1919. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: The Velveteen Rabbit
author: Margery Williams
blurb: A stuffed rabbit in a nursery wants to become Real. A short, gentle story in clear, simple sentences.
note: Published in 1922 and the author died in 1944, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: William Nicholson, the Velveteen Rabbit, illustration for The Velveteen Rabbit, 1922. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Winnie-the-Pooh
author: A. A. Milne
blurb: Ten stories about a bear of very little brain, Christopher Robin, Piglet and Eeyore. Mostly short dialogue, and the jokes work well for learners.
note: Published in 1926, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Ivan Shishkin and Konstantin Savitsky, Morning in a Pine Forest, 1889. Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
blurb: Alice follows a White Rabbit down a hole into a world where the rules keep changing. Plain, funny prose, with a lot of everyday English in the talk.
note: Published in 1865 and the author died in 1898, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: John Tenniel, The White Rabbit, illustration for Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland, 1865. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
blurb: A girl from Kansas is swept away to the Land of Oz and follows the yellow brick road to find the Wizard. Short chapters in clear, direct sentences.
note: Published in 1900 and the author died in 1919, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: W. W. Denslow, Dorothy gazed thoughtfully at the Scarecrow, illustration for The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, 1900. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: The Secret Garden
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
blurb: A lonely, sour girl finds a locked garden at a big house on the Yorkshire moors. Easy to follow, with some Yorkshire dialect in the dialogue.
note: Published in 1911 and the author died in 1924, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Mary at the garden wall, cover of an early illustrated edition of The Secret Garden (Project Gutenberg eText 17396). Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Sherlock Holmes: Five Adventures
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: Five cases from The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, from A Scandal in Bohemia to The Speckled Band. Each is a complete mystery with lively dialogue.
note: Published in 1892 and the author died in 1930, so it is in the public domain worldwide. A selection: stories I, II, III, VII and VIII of the twelve in the book.
coverCredit: Sidney Paget, illustration for The Adventure of the Speckled Band, The Strand Magazine, 1892. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
blurb: Elizabeth Bennet and the proud Mr. Darcy in a comedy about money, manners and marriage. Long, balanced Regency sentences make it a real step up.
note: Published in 1813 and the author died in 1817, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Hugh Thomson, illustration for chapter 36 of Pride and Prejudice, 1894. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
blurb: An orphan grows up, becomes a governess at Thornfield Hall and finds a secret there. A first-person classic with long sentences and rich vocabulary.
note: Published in 1847 and the author died in 1855, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Edmund H. Garrett, “Show me your palm”: Jane Eyre has her fortune told, illustration for Jane Eyre, 1890. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
blurb: Nick Carraway watches his rich neighbor Jay Gatsby chase an old love on Long Island in the 1920s. A short novel, but dense and full of images.
note: Published in 1925 and the author died in 1940, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Francis Cugat, Celestial Eyes, cover of the first edition of The Great Gatsby, 1925. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
blurb: A young scientist brings a creature to life and then runs from it. Told through letters and stories inside stories, in formal nineteenth-century English.
note: Published in 1818 and the author died in 1851, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Theodor von Holst, frontispiece to the 1831 edition of Frankenstein. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
